text:
jon: Quick sync: PR to refresh streaming examples (TS/Py/Go). Goal: demonstrate cancel, resume via resume-token header, and a simple retry pattern for idempotent streams. Also fix broken anchor in streams.md.
hana: I can take Python and the docs prose. Two quick asks: show saving resume token + a tiny resume request example, and call out that resume can produce dup tokens so callers must dedupe.
kevin: I'll own the TS snippet and a lightweight test harness that fakes a chunked response. Plan: show AbortController cancel + sending X-Redwood-Resume-Token on re-request.
yelena: Go example from me. Will demonstrate context cancellation and channel-based chunk consumption. Will include header read + resume pseudo-request.
jon: Nice. Keep each example <20 lines so it fits the guide. Prefer header name X-Redwood-Resume-Token (agreed?).
hana: Agree on header name. Python sketch (using requests + tenacity for retries):
```py
# Python streaming + resume token
from tenacity import retry, wait_exponential
import requests

r = requests.post(url, stream=True)
resume = r.headers.get('X-Redwood-Resume-Token')
for chunk in r.iter_lines():
  if chunk:
    print(chunk.decode())
    # extract partial cursor if present and save

# resume pseudo-request
headers = {'X-Redwood-Resume-Token': resume}
r2 = requests.post(url, headers=headers, stream=True)
```
I'll add a tiny retry wrapper around the request for idempotent calls.
kevin: TS snippet draft:
```ts
const controller = new AbortController();
const res = await fetch('/v1/generate/stream', { signal: controller.signal });
for await (const piece of asyncStreamIter(res.body)) {
  console.log(piece.text);
  if (piece.cursor) saveCursor(piece.cursor);
}
// cancel
controller.abort();
// resume example
await fetch('/v1/generate/stream', { headers: { 'X-Redwood-Resume-Token': savedCursor } });
```
I'll attach a tiny test that asserts the resume header is sent on retry.
yelena: Go draft:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
defer cancel()
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", url, body)
resp, _ := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
resume := resp.Header.Get("X-Redwood-Resume-Token")
scanner := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)
for scanner.Scan() { fmt.Println(scanner.Text()) }
// resume:
req2, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", url, nil)
req2.Header.Set("X-Redwood-Resume-Token", resume)
```
I'll tidy error handling and add a note about de-duplication.
devdocs-bot: heads-up: streams.md currently references an outdated section id /docs/streams#legacy-streams (404). Filing quickfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4890
jon: Thanks bot. Editorial asks: add one-line note next to each snippet: "Resuming may replay tokens; dedupe on client." And a one-sentence explanation of when resume is safe (idempotent outputs or tolerant merges).
hana: Will add that and include a tiny diagram bullet list: save token -> re-request with header -> merge/dedupe.
kevin: I'll push TS + test by EOD and tag @hana for review. Can someone review the test mocking approach? I plan to use node-fetch + a ReadableStream mock.
yelena: I can review Go. Also suggest linking to SDK streaming helpers when we merge so users see higher-level wrappers.
jon: Plan: merge docs PR + SDK snippet PRs together. Target: Friday EOD. If delayed, mark as docs-blocker in PR description. Thanks everyone."
